stem: Which wheeze pattern most favours asthma over viral wheeze in a school-aged child?

options.text: Wheeze only with respiratory tract infections
Fine crackles with or without wheeze in a child under 2 years

explanation: Regular wheeze is the pattern that most favours asthma over viral wheeze. In contrast, viral wheeze is typically linked to respiratory tract infections.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: 3.2 Chronic Airway Problems

optionExplanations.A: Correct because regular wheeze is the pattern listed for asthma.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because wheeze only with respiratory tract infections is more consistent with viral wheeze.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because fine crackles with or without wheeze in a child under 2 years suggests bronchiolitis, not asthma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because this describes the lack of a specific investigation for viral wheeze, not a feature favouring asthma.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because outgrowing symptoms by 6 years is more in keeping with viral wheeze than asthma.
